passages.original: nam deauratam a iam quae est in capsario meo, cum duobus calicibus aureis, et cruce simililer aurea, quam Mabuinus fecit, Ecclesiae meae do, lego. Simul et omnes libros meos, praeter Evangeliorum librum, quem scripsit Hilarius quondam Pictaviensis sacerdes, quem tibi Eufronio fratri et consacerdoti, dilectissimo cum præfata theca do, lego, volo, statuo. Memor esto mei, Amen.
passages.english: For the gilded [...] which is in my coffer, with two golden chalices, and a cross likewise of gold, which Mabuinus made, I give [and] bequeath to my Church. Together also all my books, except the book of the Gospels which Hilary, formerly bishop of Poitiers, wrote, which I give, bequeath, will [and] establish to you, Eufronius, my most beloved brother and fellow bishop, with the aforementioned case. Be mindful of me. Amen.
passages.notes: "deauratam a iam" appears corrupt; perhaps a noun such as "capsam" or "thecam" (gilded box/case) is intended, but the object cannot be identified with certainty, so it is marked as lost. "simililer" read as "similiter" and "sacerdes" as "sacerdos". "Sacerdos" and "consacerdos" here very likely mean bishop and fellow bishop, as in late antique usage; Hilary of Poitiers was a bishop. "Cum praefata theca" probably refers back to the silver reliquary case mentioned just before the passage. Mabuinus is not identified.
